chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said:

I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and behold, he was in his garden, holding a spade in his hand, and he was using it to open the water (flow), and he was wearing a shirt resembling cotton cloth, as if it were stitched to him due to its tightness.

key_terms.الْكَرَابِيس: Cotton cloth or fabric (specifically a type of coarse cotton)
key_terms.حَائِط: Garden or enclosed plot of land
key_terms.مِسْحَاة: A type of spade or hoe used for digging

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Imam al-Sadiq's tight shirt and spade teach about the Imams' lifestyle?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* depicts Imam al-Sadiq (as) personally managing irrigation with a *misbah* (scoop), clad in a simple, tight-fitting *karabis* shirt, highlighting the practical aspect of *tadarru' fi al-riqq* (modesty in sustenance). It serves as a normative model for the Shia community, emphasizing that spiritual leadership does not preclude manual labor or the acceptance of material simplicity, thereby validating the dignity of work and the avoidance of ostentatious wealth. This scene reinforces the principle that the Imams' lifestyle was grounded in accessibility and humility, countering notions of aristocratic detachment.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> was by a wall of his<sup>asws</sup> and in his<sup>asws</sup> hand was a spade, and he<sup>asws</sup> was opening the water (way) with it, and upon him<sup>asws</sup> was a shirt of cotton threads, as if it was stitched upon him<sup>asws</sup> due to its tightness.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Sinan from ‘Isma’il ibn Jabir who has said the following: “

I once visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and found him inside his walls with a shovel in his hand. He was opening the waterway. His shirt was of a fabric made of thick cotton threads (karabis) which was of very small size for him.”
